question.problem:
The region below enclosed by the curves $y=\sqrt x$ and $y=x$ is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the line $y=1.$ Find the volume of the resulting solid. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/362a92640ed68dfd5fa85f0338d95233003e9f8a1b059a5dffa2cda243a1411b.png)
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation:

$$
\eqalign{
 		x & =\sqrt x  \[3pt]
 		x-\sqrt x & = 0 \[3pt]
 		\sqrt x \left(\sqrt x - 1\right) &= 0 \[3pt]
 			x& = 0, 1
	}
$$

Hence, our limits of integration are from $x=0$ to $x=1.$

Now, let's draw our vertical arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/5456bed18c03e823c8e9388571b5671f5f476f5caa1085793314b57080b2b07c.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $y=\sqrt{x},$ and

- *leaves* though the outer curver $y=x.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $y=x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/5136903876ed5ea811ebf28e0da905b5029b2c9311527fce9d0fed8e7bd1dd46.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(1)-(x)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[1-x]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $y=\sqrt{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/c850643bb1c315d0516eff55d6270078504c1c98687cfac40e0c9b4b2c771b7c.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(1)-(\sqrt{x})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[1-\sqrt{x}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\eqalign{
V &= {\color{blue}V_{\text{outer}}} - {\color{brown}V_{\text{inner}}} \[5pt]
 		& = \pi \int_0^1 [1-x]^2 - \pi \int_0^1 [1-\sqrt x]^2\,\textrm d x \[5pt]
 		& = \pi \int_0^1 \left((1-x)^2 - (1-\sqrt x)^2\right) \,\textrm d x \[5pt]
 		& = \pi \int_0^1 (x^2-3x+2\sqrt x) \,\,\textrm d x \[5pt]
 		& = \pi\left. \left( \dfrac {1} 3 x^3 - \dfrac{3}{2} x^2 + \dfrac{4}{3} x^{3/2 } \ \right)\right|_0^1\[5pt] 
 		& =  \pi \left[\left( \dfrac {1}3 (1)^3 - \dfrac{3}{2}(1)^2  + \dfrac{4 }{3}(1)^{3/2 } \right) - (0) \right]\[5pt]
 		& =  \pi \left(\dfrac{1}3 - \dfrac{3}{2} +\dfrac{4}{3} \right)\[5pt]
 		& = \dfrac {\pi}{6} .
 		}
$$
